solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country set — a bit tactless unfortunately

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a tactless remark about a group of countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the twelve letters of A BIT TACTLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are grouped together as a collection of nations on one sea.

clue.text: A supporter overacting as Biblical character

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports, a common crossword trick
a ham is an actor who overacts, and to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a hammy performance as a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' is not a fan but the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch of Genesis, father of Isaac, is a central figure of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Preacher on box in the Levant, not hard — member looking up is captivated!

indicators.note: something captivated is held prisoner, so these letters are held inside the others
not hard says the letter standing for hard is left out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: the eastern Mediterranean region
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up says the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb, one of the body's members
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV preacher broadcasting in the Middle East, with an exclamation at a member of the audience gazing up enthralled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is British slang for television, so 'on box' belongs to the definition. 'not hard' drops a letter, 'looking up' turns the limb round in this down clue, and 'captivated' holds it with 'is' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist who preaches through television broadcasts is a preacher on the box, British slang for TV.

clue.text: Bring up film — the girl's a nonentity

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up a word raises it from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film or picture
her is the possessive belonging to a girl

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an actress: show the film, she is nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher in the figurative sense is a person of no importance, literally a zero.

clue.text: Travel after nice surprise includes certain valuable objects

indicators.note: after says the travel word comes after the rest in the answer
includes says the second word is held within the first

parts.note: a treat is a pleasant surprise
sure means certain
to rove is to travel about

explanation.surface: A trip following a pleasant surprise brings with it some precious items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts the word for certain inside the treat, and 'after' places the travel word last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard of buried gold or silver found with no known owner is a classic example of precious items.

clue.text: Note about kid's large family?

indicators.note: about says the note goes round the other word

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to kid is to tease or rib someone; the 's is just the clue's linking

explanation.surface: A comment on a child's big extended family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' means tease, not child. The question mark admits a tribe is only loosely a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a social group of related families with common ancestry, a very extended clan.

clue.text: Extraordinary street where there's shooting?

parts.note: a shooting range is a place for firing guns

explanation.surface: A remarkable road on which gunfire is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and extraordinary both describe something unusual or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Welcome cold shower

explanation.surface: A bracing dousing offered as a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to greet someone and the frozen pellets that fall like rain.

clue.text: Trouble envelops voting system for period

indicators.note: envelops says one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
PR is proportional representation, an electoral system

explanation.surface: Political trouble surrounds an electoral system for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'envelops' wraps the trouble word round proportional representation; 'period' is the definition, a stretch of time rather than a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year is a span of time.

clue.text: First seaside attraction to include rock, English made, at outset

indicators.note: to include says the attraction holds the other letters

parts.note: a pier is a feature of British seaside resorts, often with amusements

indicators.note: at outset says only the opening letter of each of these words is used

explanation.surface: A beach attraction featuring stick rock, the British seaside sweet, made locally from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at outset' takes the heads of three words, and 'to include' puts them inside the attraction. 'First' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means foremost or leading, as in premier division.

clue.text: Unorthodox healer, very involved in Channel port

indicators.note: involved says the letter for very is wound into the middle of the rest
unorthodox means unconventional, so these letters are set out in a non-standard order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An alternative therapist is deeply caught up in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodox' rearranges HEALER, and 'involved' puts V inside: LEHA-V-RE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major French port on the English Channel at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Say no more — extremely elite name brings lustre!

parts.note: SH is the call for silence

indicators.note: extremely says only the extremes of the word, its outer letters, are used

explanation.surface: Hush, it's enough to say an elite name gives something its shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen and lustre both mean a soft glossy shine on a surface.

clue.text: Compiler coming into money: bond

indicators.note: coming into says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a unit of money
the setter of a crossword, the compiler, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A crossword setter inherits money and puts it in a bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming into money' suggests an inheritance, but 'coming into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement binds things together, so it is a bond, both literally and figuratively.

clue.text: Show great tenderness for teacher? I shall to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pupil asks whether they should be kind to their teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to hold them dear and treat them with deep affection.

clue.text: Day nursery somewhat mediocre, cheap

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a childcare centre is second-rate and inexpensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a place where young children are looked after during working hours.

clue.text: Church with more suitable section of book

parts.note: apter is the comparative of apt, meaning suitable

explanation.surface: A church that is better fitted to a part of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter is one of the main divisions of a book.

clue.text: Pairs originally from Bolshoi lead Roman dance

indicators.note: pairs originally says the opening two letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Dancing couples from the Bolshoi Ballet lead a Roman dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of Bolshoi, lead and Roman give BO-LE-RO.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a Spanish dance in triple time, also famous through Ravel's piece.

clue.text: Remove answer in Gaelic language

indicators.note: in says the answer letter is placed inside the language name

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: An instruction to delete a reply written in Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete, removing it entirely.

clue.text: Fancy cereal used regularly in African city

indicators.note: used regularly says every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A posh breakfast cereal is a regular choice in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: In contest surpass inaccurate people

parts.note: a guess that is out is wide of the mark, inaccurate
a race is a people or ethnic group

explanation.surface: A competitor beats a field of careless rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrace a rival is to beat them in a race, finishing ahead.

clue.text: Regret about old currency unit

indicators.note: about here says the word is turned round, read the other way

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Remorse over a bygone currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the regret word round. The surface hints at a lost old coin, but 'old' only supplies a letter and the definition is a current currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the single currency used across much of the European Union.

clue.text: Popular policy retaining Conservative slant

indicators.note: retaining says the popular-plus-policy letters keep the other letter inside them

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A well-liked Tory policy is said to have a bias.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline is a slope, so it is a slant in the physical sense.

clue.text: Swimmer heading away from Beatrix?

indicators.note: heading away from says the first letter, the head, is lost

parts.note: Beatrix Potter wrote the Peter Rabbit children's books

explanation.surface: A swimmer leaving Beatrix behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname POTTER, from the author Beatrix Potter, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an aquatic mammal, an excellent swimmer.

clue.text: At work rather hot tea leads to conversation?

indicators.note: something at work is busy or in operation, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: At the office, a rather hot cup of tea prompts a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a frank, intimate talk between two people.
